:::{#def-sigma-algebra}
#### $\sigma$-algebra

A **$\sigma$-algebra** on a set $S$
is a [collection](sets-functions.qmd#def-collection) $\mathscr{S}$ of [subsets](sets-functions.qmd#def-subset) of $S$
that satisfies:

- $\mathscr{S}$ contains $S$ itself.
- For each set $A$ in $\mathscr{S}$,
  $\mathscr{S}$ contains its [complement](sets-functions.qmd#def-complement) $S \setminus A$.
- For each [sequence](sets-functions.qmd#def-sequence) $A_1, A_2, \ldots$ of sets in $\mathscr{S}$,
  $\mathscr{S}$ contains their union $\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-sigma-field}
#### $\sigma$-field

Other sources call a $\sigma$-algebra a **$\sigma$-field**
(see [Wikipedia: $\sigma$-algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%CE%A3-algebra)).
For example, @billingsley1995probability uses "$\sigma$-field".
The two names mean the same thing.

:::
